title: HCL Tech Q2 Earnings Due Today: Six Signals Investors Will Watch
excerpt: Results land after market close Monday with the stock 33% off its high — analysts expect 2–3% revenue growth and a guidance call that could reset the AI narrative.
body:
• HCL Technologies reports second-quarter results after market close on Monday, October 12 — its board met October 8 to approve the numbers and consider an interim dividend.
  • Brokerages expect 2.4–3% quarter-on-quarter revenue growth in constant currency and an EBIT margin expansion of 70–120 basis points, to roughly 18.1%.
  • The watch items: whether management raises its 1–4% FY27 revenue growth guidance, how fast AI revenue is scaling (up 62.1% year-on-year to $171 million in Q1), and the $9 million acquisition of Croatia's Robotiq.ai.
  • What this means for you: HCLTech shares sit about 33% below their 52-week high on US green-card and AI-disruption fears — the guidance call will show whether the selloff is overdone. Consensus revenue range: ₹35,443–36,012.8 crore.

HCL Technologies reports its second-quarter results after the market closes on Monday, October 12, and the numbers land at a fraught moment for Indian IT. The sector is caught between two anxieties — clients demanding AI-driven productivity discounts, and Washington's crackdown on skilled-worker mobility — and HCLTech's stock, down roughly 33% from its 52-week high, reflects both. Here are the six signals analysts say will decide whether the quarter reassures or rattles investors.

1. Revenue growth: the 2–3% test

PL Capital expects constant-currency revenue growth of 2.4% quarter-on-quarter (2.3% in dollar terms), with 1.2% organic growth plus contributions from the Jaspersoft and HPE Telco acquisitions. Motilal Oswal is slightly more bullish at 3% services-revenue growth in constant currency, roughly a percentage point of it from the two acquisitions. The Q1 FY27 baseline: revenue of ₹34,579 crore (up 13.9% year-on-year) and net income of ₹4,624 crore (up 20.3%). Consensus puts quarterly revenue between ₹35,443 crore and ₹36,012.8 crore.

2. Margins: expansion on FX and scale

"Deals and M&A: the Robotiq.ai bet New deal bookings are expected at $3–3.5 billion in total contract value, following a record $2.4 billion in Q1."

Nuvama expects EBIT margins to expand about 70 basis points quarter-on-quarter on revenue growth and a foreign-exchange tailwind; Motilal Oswal sees a bigger 120-basis-point jump to roughly 18.1%, helped by the seasonally strong second quarter. Either outcome would keep HCLTech inside its 17.5–18.5% full-year margin band — but at the upper end of expectations, which matters because AI-driven pricing pressure is the sector's central worry.

3. Profit growth: mid-teens to low-20s

Nuvama forecasts net profit growth of 15.9% year-on-year (6.2% quarter-on-quarter); Motilal Oswal is more optimistic at 21.3% year-on-year. Either way, profit growth outpacing revenue growth — the signature of a cost-disciplined quarter — is the bar.

4. Guidance: hold or raise?

Current FY27 guidance is 1–4% constant-currency revenue growth (1.5–4.5% for services) with EBIT margins of 17.5–18.5%. Nuvama expects a guidance revision; PL Capital thinks management will hold the mid-range of its organic guidance. With the stock 33% below its high, a raised outlook would be the clearest signal the AI headwinds are manageable. FinBrooks' preview flags this as the make-or-break variable.

5. The AI revenue ramp

HCLTech says AI-led revenue is still under 5% of total — but its Advanced AI revenue jumped 62.1% year-on-year to $171 million in Q1 FY27, and management admits it is passing AI productivity gains through to clients, pressuring traditional pricing. The company added RPA capabilities to HCLSoftware's UnO Agentic platform and opened an AI hub in South Africa. Investors want to know: is AI cannibalizing the core faster than it builds the new business? Moody's preview data compiles the full analyst spread.

6. Deals and M&A: the Robotiq.ai bet

New deal bookings are expected at $3–3.5 billion in total contract value, following a record $2.4 billion in Q1. On the M&A front, HCLTech is acquiring Croatia-based Robotiq.ai for €9 million through HCLSoftware, with closing expected in November 2026 — a small but telling bet on agentic AI tooling. The stock slipped about 1.5% on the announcement.

Why it matters beyond the quarter

HCLTech is one of the eight firms suspended from the US Labor Department's PERM green-card programme last week, and it reports into a market that has sold Indian IT on fears of both AI disruption and immigration restrictions. For the large NRI investor base that holds Indian IT as a portfolio anchor, Monday's call is less about one quarter's numbers and more about the answer to the sector's defining question: can India's IT giants price AI productivity into growth instead of margin compression? The guidance number will tell.
